title: Experience-based Knowledge Correction for Robust Planning in Minecraft
claim: Pretrained models hold flawed knowledge of task structure and cannot repair it from failure feedback, repeating the same errors.
layout: 4 panels: graphs stacked left, self-correction flows right, shared legend
description: A legend column on the far left explains arrow and highlight colors: correct, missed and redundant dependencies, hallucinated items, wrong knowledge, and ground truth. Next to it, panel (a) shows the true Minecraft item dependency graph with black arrows between block icons. Below it, panel (b) shows the LLM-predicted graph, with extra red dashed redundant arrows, orange missed arrows and a red bug icon marking a hallucinated item. A dashed vertical line separates these from two wide panels on the right. Panels (c) and (d) each show a left-to-right self-correction loop: prior attempt (speech bubble with an LLM logo), then a correction prompt document icon, then the next attempt. The next attempt repeats the same wrong knowledge, highlighted in red, and ends in a red 'Fail!'. Panel (c) covers dependencies and panel (d) covers actions. Panel backgrounds are tinted blue, green and purple.
caption: An LLM exhibits flawed planning knowledge and fails at self-correction. (b) The dependency graph predicted by Qwen2.5-VL-7B [ref] contains multiple errors (e.g., missed dependencies, hallucinated items) compared to (a) the ground truth. (c, d) The LLM fails to correct its flawed knowledge about dependencies and actions from failure feedbacks, often repeating the same errors. See [ref] for the full prompts and LLM's self-correction examples.
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based planning has advanced embodied agents in long-horizon environments such as Minecraft, where acquiring latent knowledge of goal (or item) dependencies and feasible actions is critical. However, LLMs often begin with flawed priors and fail to correct them through prompting, even with feedback. We present XENON (eXpErience-based kNOwledge correctioN), an agent that algorithmically revises knowledge from experience, enabling robustness to flawed priors and sparse binary feedback. XENON integrates two mechanisms: Adaptive Dependency Graph, which corrects item dependencies using past successes, and Failure-aware Action Memory, which corrects action knowledge using past failures. Together, these components allow XENON to acquire complex dependencies despite limited guidance. Experiments across multiple Minecraft benchmarks show that XENON outperforms prior agents in both knowledge learning and long-horizon planning. Remarkably, with only a 7B open-weight LLM, XENON surpasses agents that rely on much larger proprietary models. Project page: https://sjlee-me.github.io/XENON
